title: RTE+RRTMGP radiation code (CESM3, E3SM, ICON)
summary: 6 interpolation/indexing bugs, all now fixed; the worst (#425, in every release since v1.0) is triggered when a key gas is zero or near zero: the gas keeps absorbing, so runs that remove a gas (for example CO2-removal experiments, or configurations that switch a gas off) understate its effect by 70–80%.
about: RTE+RRTMGP is the radiative-transfer code that computes how sunlight and infrared radiation are absorbed and emitted by gases, clouds and aerosols. It is the radiation scheme in several major climate models, including CESM3, E3SM and ICON.

title: COARE air–sea flux algorithm (CMEPS, E3SM, NorESM)
target: COARE air–sea flux algorithm (CMEPS, E3SM, NorESM)
summary: Sign error in the COARE flux code
about: The COARE algorithm calculates the exchange of heat, moisture and momentum between the ocean surface and the atmosphere (air–sea fluxes). Versions of it are used in the coupling code of climate models such as CESM (CMEPS), E3SM and NorESM.

title: climate_indices (SPI, Pearson III)
summary: Zero-rain months counted twice in SPI
about: climate_indices is a Python package that computes drought indices such as the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), which expresses rainfall over a period as a number of standard deviations from normal.

title: R SPEI package (spi/spei)
summary: Zero-rain adjustment overwritten, so SPI returns −Inf (versions 1.8.0–1.8.1, 2022–26); 47+ papers used it
about: SPEI is the R package, written by the index's developers, that computes the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and the Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), two of the most widely used drought indices.

title: xclim SPI (Ouranos)
summary: Default 3-parameter gamma fit collapses its location onto the sample minimum (SPI −8.21)
about: xclim is a Python library from Ouranos (Montreal) for computing climate indices from model and observational data. Its SPI function converts rainfall totals into a standardized drought index.

title: martinvonk/SPEI (Python)
summary: prob_zero=True counts zeros twice, biasing SPI high
about: martinvonk/SPEI is a Python package for computing standardized drought indices (SPI, SPEI) from rainfall and evaporation series.

title: climdex.pcic ETCCDI indices (feeds HadEX3, CMIP6 index sets)
target: climdex.pcic ETCCDI indices (feeds HadEX3, CMIP6 index sets)
summary: WSDI/CSDI never got the Zhang et al. (2005) in-base bootstrap, leaving a spurious base-period step
about: climdex.pcic is the R package from the Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium that computes the 27 ETCCDI climate-extremes indices (hot days, warm spells, heavy rain and so on). Its output feeds the HadEX3 global extremes dataset and CMIP6 index sets.

title: CDO etccdi operators
summary: Same missing bootstrap; rx1daymon/rx5daymon return unaggregated data; other bugs
about: CDO (Climate Data Operators) is a widely used command-line toolkit for processing climate model and gridded data. Its etccdi operators compute the standard ETCCDI climate-extremes indices.

title: ClimPACT (WMO indices software)
summary: Heatwave indices without bootstrap; SPI zeros double-counted; parameter typo
about: ClimPACT is the World Meteorological Organization's software for computing climate indices (extremes, heatwaves, drought) from station data, used by national weather services.

title: pyMannKendall (Python)
summary: Yue–Wang test default rejects ~47% of pure-noise series at the 5% level
about: pyMannKendall is a Python package for the Mann–Kendall trend test and its variants, which test whether a time series has a monotonic trend, including versions that correct for autocorrelation.

title: modifiedmk (R) mmky()
summary: Same all-lags flaw since v1.1.0 (2018)
about: modifiedmk is an R package of Mann–Kendall trend tests modified for serially correlated data. Its mmky() function implements the Yue–Wang variance correction.

title: Hamed–Rao test default (pyMannKendall, modifiedmk)
summary: About 2× the nominal false-positive rate on white noise
about: The Hamed–Rao test is a version of the Mann–Kendall trend test that inflates the test's variance to allow for autocorrelation. It is implemented in pyMannKendall and modifiedmk.

title: xsdba / xclim.sdba QDM bias adjustment (Ouranos)
summary: Ranks wrong when dry days tie, so adjusted precipitation blows up 4–9× for dry-biased models
about: xsdba (formerly xclim.sdba) is Ouranos's Python library for statistical bias adjustment of climate model output. Quantile Delta Mapping (QDM) corrects a model's distribution against observations while preserving its projected changes.

title: xclim PET (Thornthwaite) and heat index
summary: Heat index recomputed each year halves warming-driven PET increases; bare Rothfusz heat index
about: xclim's potential evapotranspiration (PET) functions estimate how much water the atmosphere could take up; the Thornthwaite method uses temperature only. Its heat index combines temperature and humidity into an apparent temperature.

title: PCMDI Metrics Package (CMIP benchmarking)
summary: rms_xyt redefined in the xCDAT port; always biased low
about: The PCMDI Metrics Package (PMP), from Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, is the standard software for benchmarking CMIP climate models against observations.

title: climpred (decadal prediction verification)
summary: Uninitialized reference uses single-member skill, overstating the value of initialization; bootstrap false positives 68–73%
about: climpred is a Python package for verifying initialized decadal and seasonal climate predictions, including comparing them with uninitialized (free-running) model simulations.

title: Skyborn (optimal fingerprinting)
summary: Model-uncertainty covariance keeps only the diagonal; 90% intervals cover the truth 67% of the time
about: Skyborn is a Python package for optimal fingerprinting, the regression method used to detect and attribute climate change to particular causes (greenhouse gases, aerosols, natural factors).

title: tcpyPI (hurricane potential intensity)
summary: Published fix never implemented; zero-CAPE outflow case
about: tcpyPI is the Python implementation of the potential-intensity algorithm (Bister and Emanuel), which estimates the maximum intensity a hurricane could reach given ocean and atmospheric conditions.

title: rwwa (World Weather Attribution R code)
summary: Bootstrap refits silently switch optimizer and often fail for shift-scale fits; core statistics hold
about: rwwa is World Weather Attribution's R code for extreme-event attribution: it fits extreme-value distributions that shift with global warming and estimates how much climate change altered an event's likelihood.

title: NCAR MMM-physics (WRF/MPAS) KIM TOFD option
summary: Friction velocity 28–41% high; uninitialized variable
about: MMM-physics is NCAR's shared library of physics schemes for the WRF and MPAS weather models. The KIM TOFD option represents turbulent orographic form drag (the drag of small-scale terrain on the wind).

title: MetPy vorticity/divergence
summary: Map-factor error grows toward the poles (~10,000× at pole rows)
about: MetPy is a widely used Python library for meteorological calculations. Its vorticity and divergence functions compute rotation and spreading of the wind from gridded data.

title: wrf-python updraft helicity
summary: Divides by the map factor instead of multiplying (bias 1/m²)
about: wrf-python is NCAR's Python library for post-processing WRF model output. Updraft helicity is a diagnostic used to identify rotating thunderstorms (supercells).

title: GeoCAT-comp seasonal averages
summary: Partial DJF seasons returned silently; winter trends biased up to ~35%
about: GeoCAT-comp is NCAR's Python library of geoscience computations (the successor to NCL functions). Its seasonal-average routines compute DJF, MAM, JJA and SON means.

title: GeoCAT-comp gradient()
summary: Outputs in reverse of documented order; official moisture-convergence example wrong
about: GeoCAT-comp's gradient() function computes spatial derivatives of gridded fields, used for example in moisture-convergence calculations.

title: xCDAT seasonal averages
summary: Dropping incomplete seasons fails, or silently keeps partial DJF, for daily data
about: xCDAT (Xarray Climate Data Analysis Tools) is a Python library, developed with DOE support, for common climate-data operations such as temporal and seasonal averaging.

title: xESMF conservative regridding
summary: Polar rows corrupted for pole-centered grids (ERA5, MERRA-2, JRA-55)
about: xESMF is a Python package for regridding (interpolating) climate data between grids. Conservative regridding is meant to preserve totals such as rainfall or energy.

title: earthkit-meteo (ECMWF)
summary: Default wet-bulb potential temperature up to ~1.2 K too low
about: earthkit-meteo is ECMWF's Python library of meteorological calculations, including humidity and wet-bulb temperature functions.

title: CLIMADA (ETH) ER11 hurricane wind profile

about: CLIMADA is ETH Zurich's open-source platform for climate risk assessment. Its tropical-cyclone module models the wind field around a storm track (here the Emanuel–Rotunno 2011 profile).

title: hydroeval non-parametric KGE
summary: Tied values (zero flows) ranked by time order, biasing KGE_NP for intermittent rivers
about: hydroeval is a Python package of goodness-of-fit scores for hydrological models. The non-parametric Kling–Gupta efficiency (KGE_NP) compares simulated and observed river flows using ranks.

title: eofs / xeofs (EOF analysis)
summary: Known in-place bug (fix pending); patterns returned still weighted (doc gap)
about: eofs and xeofs are Python packages for Empirical Orthogonal Function (EOF) analysis, which finds the dominant spatial patterns of variability in climate data.

title: Global Warming Index, IGCC forcing, Zelinka ECS tables
target: Global Warming Index, IGCC forcing, Zelinka ECS tables
summary: Minor window and check slips only
about: Three widely used reference products: the Global Warming Index (human-induced warming to date), the radiative-forcing series of the Indicators of Global Climate Change (IGCC), and Mark Zelinka's tables of climate sensitivity and feedbacks for CMIP models.

title: Clean checks: properscoring, PyKrige, thermofeel, ESMValCore, xskillscore, MBC, R SPEI PET, GEFF/xclim fire weather, dlnm heat-mortality workflow
target: Clean checks: properscoring, PyKrige, thermofeel, ESMValCore, xskillscore, MBC, R SPEI PET, GEFF/xclim fire weather, dlnm heat-mortality workflow

title: ASOS wind sensors (sonic swap 2005–09; commissioning)
summary: US steps of −6.5% (sonic) and −9% (commissioning) remove most US 1988–2010 stilling; global 1978–2010 decline (Zeng method) −2.7 → −1.9 %/decade; NH (HadISD design) −24%
about: The Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS) is the network of about 900 automated weather stations at US airports. Its wind sensors were changed from cup anemometers to sonic sensors in 2005–09; ASOS wind data feed global wind-trend studies through HadISD and ISD.

title: NOAA hourly precipitation dataset (HPD)
summary: Step at the 2012 digital upgrade (~+9–10% in hourly maxima)
about: NOAA's Hourly Precipitation Data (HPD) is the US archive of hourly rain-gauge totals from about 2,000 stations, used to study short-duration extreme rainfall and design storms (for example NOAA Atlas 14/15).

title: ICOADS R3.1 marine observations
summary: ~295,000 position-error duplicates; some HadSST4 box-months rest on misplaced copies
about: ICOADS (International Comprehensive Ocean-Atmosphere Data Set) is the main archive of ship, buoy and other marine surface observations since the 1600s. It underlies sea-surface-temperature datasets such as HadSST4 and ERSST.

title: IBTrACS tropical cyclone archive
summary: Provisional seasons run low with blank WMO winds; flag documentation out of date; otherwise clean
about: IBTrACS (International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship) is NOAA's global archive of tropical-cyclone tracks and intensities, combining the records of the world's forecast agencies.

title: ASOS dew-point sensor swap (DTS1, 2002–06)
summary: Transient drift reset; no lasting step
about: The ASOS humidity sensor (DTS1) replaced the earlier chilled-mirror dew-point sensors at US airport weather stations in 2002–06.

title: NOAA OISST v2.1
summary: Excess recent warming inflates marine-heatwave trends 7–14%
about: NOAA's Optimum Interpolation Sea Surface Temperature (OISST) v2.1 is a daily, 0.25° global map of sea-surface temperature blending satellite, ship and buoy data. It is the standard dataset for marine-heatwave studies.

title: Boers 2021 NCC (AMOC); Boulton et al. 2022 NCC (Amazon)
target: Boers 2021 NCC (AMOC); Boulton et al. 2022 NCC (Amazon)
summary: Same surrogate test overstates significance; headlines largely survive
about: Boers (2021, Nature Climate Change) reported early-warning signals that the Atlantic overturning circulation (AMOC) is losing stability; Boulton et al. (2022, Nature Climate Change) reported the same for the Amazon rainforest. Both use rising variance and autocorrelation tested against surrogate data.

title: Kossin et al. 2020, PNAS (major-hurricane share; IPCC AR6)
target: Kossin et al. 2020, PNAS (major-hurricane share; IPCC AR6)
summary: Clustering understated; 1979–2017 change not significant (p = 0.10); trend holds through 2024
about: Kossin et al. (2020, PNAS) reported that the global proportion of tropical-cyclone intensity estimates at major-hurricane strength (Category 3+) rose between 1979–1997 and 1998–2017, using a homogenized satellite record. The result is cited in the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report.

title: Ali et al. 2026, npj CAS (hurricane rainfall scaling)

summary: Headline 21%/K not reproduced (12%); within-storm ~2%/K
about: Ali et al. (2026, npj Climate and Atmospheric Science) estimated how hurricane rainfall increases with sea-surface temperature, reporting about 21% more rain per degree of warming.

title: Clean checks: Mauritsen 2025 (energy imbalance doubled), Nerem 2018 (sea-level acceleration), Dangendorf 2026 (coastal extremes), Xu 2026 CEE (drought), Guerreiro 2018 (hourly extremes), IGCC 2025 marine-heatwave indicator
target: Clean checks: Mauritsen 2025 (energy imbalance doubled), Nerem 2018 (sea-level acceleration), Dangendorf 2026 (coastal extremes), Xu 2026 CEE (drought), Guerreiro 2018 (hourly extremes), IGCC 2025 marine-heatwave indicator
summary: Claims hold under independent tests (6 studies)
about: Six widely cited studies we tested independently and found to hold: Earth's energy imbalance doubling (Mauritsen 2025), sea-level acceleration (Nerem 2018), coastal extremes (Dangendorf 2026), drought (Xu 2026), hourly rainfall extremes (Guerreiro 2018) and the IGCC 2025 marine-heatwave indicator.

title: lmoments3 1.0.8 (Ouranos; L-moment engine behind xclim PWM fits) and standard_precip SPI
target: lmoments3 1.0.8 (Ouranos; L-moment engine behind xclim PWM fits) and standard_precip SPI
summary: Wakeby distribution: quantile/CDF/PDF use the scale-dependent γ unscaled and reject valid δ<0, so 77–85% of fitted 100-yr values are NaN or off by ~50×; standard_precip SPI with dist_type='wak' inherits it (half of months NaN, 78% 'severe drought' vs 5%)
about: lmoments3 is the Python library (maintained by Ouranos) that fits extreme-value distributions by L-moments; it is the engine behind xclim's distribution fits. standard_precip is a Python package for computing the Standardized Precipitation Index.

title: Hugonnet et al. 2021, Nature (accelerated global glacier mass loss, 2000–2019)
target: Hugonnet et al. 2021, Nature (accelerated global glacier mass loss, 2000–2019)
summary: The 95% interval on the mass-loss acceleration (48 ± 16 Gt/yr per decade) was formed by doubling a 1σ interval from a regression with ~2 degrees of freedom; the correct t-based 95% half-width is ~1.64× larger (about ±26). The acceleration remains significant at the corrected level; the author notes conservative assumptions elsewhere (temporal decorrelation, density conversion) likely offset the narrower interval.
about: Hugonnet et al. (2021, Nature) mapped thinning of nearly all of the world's ~220,000 glaciers from satellite elevation data and reported that glacier mass loss accelerated over 2000–2019.

title: NASA MERRA-2 corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) over Australia
target: NASA MERRA-2 corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) over Australia
summary: About a 20% dry step from 2016 in PRECTOTCORR over Australia, inherited from the CPC Unified gauge analysis (CPCU) that MERRA-2 uses to correct land precipitation. CPCU's own gauge-count field shows Australia lost about 95% of its gauges in two steps (2007–08 and 2015–16, e.g. E Australia ~590 → 90). GPCP and GPCC do not show the step, and a gauge-independent reanalysis (NCEP R1) confirms it sits in CPCU.
about: MERRA-2 is NASA's global atmospheric reanalysis. Its corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), which drives the land surface, is adjusted toward NOAA's CPC Unified daily gauge analysis over land.

title: E-OBS v34.0e precipitation, northern Morocco from February 2006
target: E-OBS v34.0e precipitation, northern Morocco from February 2006
summary: Every Moroccan precipitation station in E-OBS within 34–39°N, 10–3.5°W stops on 7 February 2006 (Tangier airport, Al Hoceima, Taza and Rabat-Salé); afterwards the only station on the African side is Ceuta, and the Moroccan grid cells are filled from distant stations. From then on those cells change character while the Iberian cells do not: their October–March maximum daily rainfall (box mean) averages 33 mm in the 2000s, 48 mm in the 2010s and 55 mm in the 2020s (Iberian cells 23, 27, 29 mm), and their E-OBS ensemble spread on wet days rises from 5.3–6.1 mm before 2005 to 6.9–8.0 mm, while Iberia's falls. The Moroccan cells carry about half of the rainfall-extremes trend over the box used by World Weather Attribution Report No. 83. Whether rainfall over northern Morocco really changed cannot be told from E-OBS after 2006.

title: E-OBS v34.0e precipitation, Greece 2005–2014
summary: Public ECA&D Greek stations with near-complete years fall from about 10 to 1–2 in 2005–2013 and return to 5–7 from 2014. E-OBS Greek precipitation drops by about 35–45% over exactly those years against both CPC Unified (ratio 0.71–0.83 → 0.40–0.60 → 0.60–0.84) and GPCP (0.55–0.66 → 0.32–0.48 → 0.56–0.79). In 2006 E-OBS has 239 mm over the box, against 599 mm (CPC) and 736 mm (GPCP).

title: Koutsoyiannis et al. 2023, Sci (temperature–CO2 causality, “Hens and Eggs”)
target: Koutsoyiannis et al. 2023, Sci (temperature–CO2 causality, “Hens and Eggs”)
summary: The paper's impulse-response causality test, applied to 12-month differences of temperature and ln CO2, reports “temperature leads CO2” in a synthetic world where CO2 causes all of the long-term warming by construction (100% of runs; 95–100% with 1-, 5- and 10-year differences), and gives the same answer in a world where temperature drives CO2. Differencing removes the slow, emissions-driven part of CO2, so the test sees only the well-known interannual response of the CO2 growth rate to temperature. It cannot tell the two causal directions apart, so the paper's conclusion of a unidirectional link from temperature to CO2 does not follow from it. The opposite result in CMIP6 is expected by construction, because those runs prescribe CO2 concentrations.
verdict: Method weakness (test cannot detect CO2 → temperature)

title: Liu et al. 2026, Nat Commun (intense tropical-cyclone season length)
target: Liu et al. 2026, Nat Commun (intense tropical-cyclone season length)
summary: The intense-TC season length (span between the 1.5th and 98.5th percentiles of occurrence dates in 3-year windows) grows with the number of storms in the window even when their timing does not change, and intense-TC counts rose in every basin over 1980–2023. The paper's own lengths correlate 0.50–0.88 with the window count. Drawing dates from each basin's fixed 1980–2023 distribution with the observed yearly counts produces “lengthening” of about 2–16 days/decade by itself. Calibrated against that null, only the western North Pacific stays significant (p ≈ 0.03); the hemispheric trends do not (NH p ≈ 0.08, SH p ≈ 0.6). The Mann–Kendall test on overlapping 3-year windows rejects at the 5% level in 24–75% of no-change cases.

title: pyextremes: missing data biased return values low
summary: Gaps in a record made the peaks-over-threshold event rate too low and let partly observed blocks count as full blocks, so return values came out too low. Fixed by the developer in v2.7.0 (new observed_duration and min_block_count options).

fix.scope: Forward only. Results computed with affected versions are not corrected; rerun with the fixed version or later. Use the new observed_duration and min_block_count options on gappy records.

about: pyextremes is a Python library for extreme-value analysis, used to estimate return levels (for example the 100-year flood or rainfall) from block maxima or peaks over a threshold.
